units.passage: The use of AI-generated content is not permitted in this course. Its use will result in an academic integrity violation and a zero on the assignment.\\ \\ OR\\ \\ The use of AI-generated content is allowed in this course.\\ \\ OR\\ \\ The use of AI-generated content is permitted as follows: (a) for generating a first draft or (b) for generating an outline or (c) for generating XXX.
units.why: "permitted as follows: (a) for generating a first draft or (b) for generating an outline or (c) for generating XXX" limits AI to a closed list of tasks chosen by the instructor, P107.
units.fit_note: Instructor fills in the list; first draft and outline are the example uses.

units.passage: The following uses of generative AI tools are permitted in this course:
units.why: The second template says only 'The following uses ... are permitted', a closed list of tasks chosen by the instructor: P107 (limit AI to listed tasks).
units.fit_note: A template for an instructor-chosen list of permitted uses. | Template for listing permitted uses; the restriction to a closed list is the instructor's choice.

units.passage: You may use generative AI for brainstorming and outlining only.
units.why: Strategic sample: AI 'for brainstorming and outlining only' limits AI to a closed list of tasks (P107); brainstorming alone would be P15, but 'only' makes it a task limit.
units.fit_note: Also outlining and the closed list 'only' (P107).

units.passage: It may include, but is not limited to: [1] submitting work generated by AI as one’s own without proper acknowledgement; [2] accessing or using AI tools without authorization; and [3] failure to acknowledge AI-generated contributions to an assignment or other academic work.
units.why: The second example, 'accessing or using AI tools without authorization', makes AI use misuse unless authorized. That is an authorization-required rule (P107) rather than a tier or a syllabus-silence rule.
units.fit_note: Does not say who authorizes (the 'Course AI Policy' later suggests the instructor).

units.passage: siempre que sea autorizado por sus profesores en las materias asignadas.
units.policy: Students may use AI as part of their educational experience only when authorized by their professors in the assigned courses.
units.why: Students "podrá utilizar IA ... siempre que sea autorizado por sus profesores": use is allowed only after instructor authorization, so a prior-approval default (P107); the instructor-level element resembles P04 but the default rule is the needed authorization.
units.fit_note: The authorizing party is the course instructor, which also resembles P04. | Coder A: Permission is conditional on instructor authorization, so the default is no use unless authorized. | Also resembles P04, since the authorizing party is the course instructor.

units.passage: Any unauthorized use of GenAI tools will be processed in the same manner as other academic misconduct violations under the University's Student Academic Conduct Policy." Option 2: Use of Generative AI is Permitted as Specified by the Faculty Member “The use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini, etc.) in this course is permitted only as explicitly outlined below and for specific assignments.
units.why: Option 2 says GenAI "is permitted only as explicitly outlined below and for specific assignments", permission limited to listed uses (P107).
units.fit_note: Template for instructor-specified permission per assignment.

units.passage: proper use of ChatGPT or other artificial intelligence services in this scenario would consist of the student first asking their professor if they were allowed to use ChatGPT to assist in the brainstorming process.
units.why: In the brainstorming example the student should first ask the professor and may brainstorm 'If permitted by the instructor'; permission before use, P107.
units.fit_note: Also P10 (ask first); the permitted use is brainstorming (P15).

units.passage: There are specific instances in this course where you will be allowed to use generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) to assist in your learning. Limiting AI use to specific assignments or situations helps you develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills independently, while still benefiting from AI assistance when appropriate.
units.why: Option 2 allows AI only in 'specific instances in this course' to assist learning, meaning AI is limited to listed assignments; P107 fits.

units.passage: and faculty must approve its use for coursework, supervised research, and examinations.
units.why: 'Faculty must approve its use for coursework, supervised research, and examinations', so AI use needs prior faculty approval: P107.

units.passage: here are specific instances in this course where you will be allowed to use generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) to assist in your learning.
units.why: Permissible use means 'specific instances in this course where you will be allowed to use generative' AI, limited to listed uses: P107.

units.passage: Use AI only when permitted, and make sure you cite it, even if you only use it to generate an outline or to organize your ideas.
units.why: "Use AI only when permitted" limits AI to permitted instances, so P107, must.

units.passage: Students may use AI technology for any learning, creation, or analysis, without restriction. Mixed Use – Students may use AI technology for some learning, creation, or analysis, with specifics provided in a clear and timely manner.
units.why: 'Mixed Use' lets students use AI for some tasks with specifics 'provided in a clear and timely manner'; a middle tier allowing AI only for specified uses, so P107 fits better than P05, which names the tier set itself.
units.fit_note: An option instructors may choose; the allowed tasks are specified by the instructor in the course.

units.passage: Encourage AI use in specific assignments, but not all. Students must disclose any AI assistance.
units.why: Moderate use: 'Encourage AI use in specific assignments, but not all': assignment-by-assignment permission, P04. [Reconciled: policy_type=P107.]
units.fit_note: Also a named tier (P05) and requires disclosure.

units.passage: In this course, students are permitted to use Generative AI Tools such as ChatGPT for specific assignments, as designated by the instructor.
units.why: Moderate Use permits AI 'for specific assignments, as designated by the instructor': AI allowed only where the instructor designates, P107.
units.fit_note: A sample statement for instructors to adopt, not a binding policy. | Other coder: Permission is tied to assignments the instructor designates.

units.passage: You may use AI tools to brainstorm ideas or plan your approach. However, your final work must reflect your own reasoning and analysis. AI-generated ideas are not your own and must be cited if directly included. Any uncredited AI-generated content will be treated as plagiarism and referred to the Office of Community Standards. Fall 2025 AI Allowed with Permission You may use AI tools only with prior instructor approval.
units.why: Sample 'AI Allowed with Permission': 'You may use AI tools only with prior instructor approval', permission required first, P107.

units.passage: AI may be used in specific stages of course projects: brainstorming, outlining, and editing.
units.why: 'Sometimes, and here's when': 'AI may be used in specific stages of course projects: brainstorming, outlining, and editing', a limited list of uses, P107.
units.fit_note: Limits AI to named project stages.

units.passage: If you believe a specific service is necessary for your work, you are expected to work with the relevant governing unit to evaluate it before use
units.why: Use of a discouraged foreign service requires review with the governing unit first, a prior-approval step: P107.

units.passage: This includes using the assistance of A.I. text generators to perform central requirements of an assignment (i.e., reading, synthesizing, interpreting, writing, coding, programming, etc.) without both the explicit permission of the instructor and complete attribution and citation of A.I.-assisted components.
units.policy: Students do not use A.I. text generators to perform central requirements of an assignment (reading, synthesizing, interpreting, writing, coding, programming) without both the explicit permission of the instructor and complete attribution and citation of A.I.-assisted components.
units.why: Using "A.I. text generators to perform central requirements of an assignment ... without both the explicit permission of the instructor and complete attribution and citation" is cheating; AI doing the central work needs prior instructor permission, so P107, must-not, restrict.
units.fit_note: Lists central requirements (reading, synthesizing, interpreting, writing, coding, programming); permission is required plus citation. / Also lists reading and synthesizing as central requirements and requires both permission and citation.

units.passage: As such, our use of GenAI tools will be limited and specific.
units.why: "our use of GenAI tools will be limited and specific" restricts use to defined tasks. P107 is the nearest, because this snippet gives no list.
units.fit_note: Limits use to specific assignments, tasks not listed in this excerpt. Rationale is professional knowledge in law (building conceptual understanding first) rather than novices.

units.passage: In this course, generative AI tools may only be used for specific assignments that are designated by the instructor.
units.why: Template 3 says AI 'may only be used for specific assignments that are designated by the instructor'; allowed only where designated, so P107 (limited to designated cases) rather than P04, since the default outside is a ban.

units.passage: Consult your departmental IT staff before installing AI tools or plug-ins on university owned computers.
units.why: 'Consult your departmental IT staff before installing AI tools or plug-ins on university owned computers' requires checking before installing (P107, prior approval).
units.fit_note: Consultation before installing, rather than formal approval. | Consult-before-install, not a strict approval requirement.

units.passage: Students are permitted to use advanced automated artificial intelligence or machine learning tools on assignments in this course if instructor permission is obtained in advance.
units.why: Option 2 says AI tools are allowed "if instructor permission is obtained in advance", so AI is permitted only after explicit prior approval; this is P107 (prior approval) and not P10 (asking when unsure).
